question.problem:
Using the normal approximation to the binomial distribution, approximate the probability that $35$ out of $90$ rolls of a $6$-sided die land on an even number.

*Hint: The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.00\,$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,-2.2\,$ | $\,0.0139\,$ | $\,0.0136\,$ | $\,0.0132\,$ |
| $\,-2.1\,$ | $\,0.0179\,$ | $\,0.0174\,$ | $\,0.0170\,$ |
| $\,-2.0\,$ | $\,0.0228\,$ | $\,0.0222\,$ | $\,0.0217\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Given a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ if 

- $np>5,$ and

- $n(1-p)>5,$

we can approximate $X$ as a normal random variable $Y$ with mean $\mu =np$ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p),$ that is, 

$$
Y∼N(np,np(1-p)).
$$

Here, we have $n=90$ and $p=0.5.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =90\cdot 0.5 \\  & =45 \\  & >5\,✓ \\ n(1-p) & =90\cdot (1-0.5) \\  & =45 \\  & >5.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can approximate our binomial random variable $X$ with a normal random variable $Y$ with mean

$$
\mu =np=(90)(0.5)=45
$$

and variance

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p)=(90)(0.5)(1-0.5)=22.5.
$$

That is, we can approximate $X$ by $Y∼N(45,22.5).$

Now, we can approximate the desired probability $P(X=35).$ Using a continuity correction, we have

$$
P(X=35)≈P(34.5\le Y\le 35.5).
$$

To compute this probability, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(34.5\le Y\le 35.5) & =P(\frac{34.5-45}{\sqrt{22.5}}\le Z\le \frac{35.5-45}{\sqrt{22.5}}) \\  & ≈P(-2.21\le Z\le -2.00) \\  & =P(Z\le -2.00)-P(Z<-2.21) \\  & =P(Z\le -2.00)-P(Z\le -2.21) \\  & =Φ(-2.00)-Φ(-2.21) \\  & =0.0228-0.0136 \\  & =0.0092\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
P(X=35)≈0.009.
$$

Note: Using a software package for the approximation gives a probability of $0.0092.$
